newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CSOB cuts base rate to 21 pct from 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech CSOB cuts base rate to 21 pct from 22 pct.

text.p: Czech bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. said on Tuesday it was cutting its base lending rate applicable for up to one-year credit by one percentage point to 21 percent.
The bank said in a statement it was leaving its other rates unchanged.
CSOB last changed its base rate on June 12, cutting it by three percentage points from 25 percent.

Czech commercial banks have started lowering their rates after the Czech National Bank (CNB) began to ease restrictions on access to credit which were imposed in late May during a spoeculative atack on the Czech crown.
The CNB's Lombard rate has been at 50 percent since May 16 after the previous 14 percent, and the discount rate is 13 percent, up from 10.5 percent.

The central bank, however, began easing repo rates, lowering the one-week rate to 18.5 percent on Tuesday, down from 75 percent at its peak during the currency crisis which forced the central bank to float the crown on May 28.
